transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I got myself in over my head with a historical society fundraiser. I started acting like I could run the whole thing myself—calling volunteers, making schedules, even starting quilt designs—and I promised deadlines I really couldn’t meet.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to act on?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve been busy with all of it, but not like I have to do some specific thing over and over or anything.
Have you been feeling anxious about the fundraiser or your responsibilities in general?
I don’t know… maybe a little stressed, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really thought of it as anxiety. It’s just been a lot to keep up with.
Do you feel like you need to do things perfectly?
I’m not sure I’d call it perfect. I just… don’t like things being left messy or half-done, I guess. But no, not perfect exactly.
Do you often find yourself taking on more tasks or responsibilities than others might in similar situations?

Yes… I suppose I do. With the historical society fundraiser, I kind of took it over—quilts, volunteers, schedules. I told people I’d have things done by certain times, and… looking back, I’m not sure those deadlines were realistic.
Do you feel like you have to be in charge of things to feel comfortable?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. It’s not like I need to be in charge exactly. I just feel uneasy if things aren’t clear, so I end up stepping in.
Do you feel a strong need for things to be organized or done in a specific way?
I mean… I like things to be somewhat organized. I don’t know if I’d call it a strong need. It just bothers me when things feel scattered, so I try to get them in order.
Do you think you took on so much with the fundraiser because you were worried about what others would think of you if you didn't?
I’m not sure. Maybe a little, but I don’t think that was the main thing. I just… felt like it needed to get done, and I stepped in.
Did you take on all the responsibilities with the fundraiser because you were afraid of what others might think if things didn't go well?

Not exactly. I think I just… got carried away with it. I took on the fundraiser like I could run the whole thing myself—quilts, volunteers, schedules, deadlines. I didn’t really think through whether I could actually do all of it.
Did you worry that others would think less of you if the fundraiser wasn't successful?
I don’t think that was really it. I mean… maybe I didn’t want it to go badly, but I wasn’t sitting there thinking people would think less of me.
Do you think your actions with the fundraiser were influenced by a desire to avoid others criticizing you?
I don’t know… I don’t think criticism was really what was driving it. I just kind of took it on, and then it got bigger than I expected.
Do you feel uncomfortable when things are not going according to your plans?
Sometimes, I guess. I don’t like it when things get messy, but… I’m not sure I’d say it’s a big thing for me.
Do you often worry about what other people think of you?
I mean… not often, no. I think about it sometimes like anyone does, but I don’t feel like it’s something I’m constantly worrying over.
Do you often think you're more capable of handling things than others?
At the time, yes… I guess I did. I really thought my quilt ideas could do something big for the town, like maybe I was the one person who could pull it off.
Do you often think you're more capable of handling complex situations than most other people?
I suppose I did, at least with the quilt project. I really believed those heritage quilt ideas could put our little town on the map… like it was something only I could make happen.
Do you often feel like your abilities or ideas are superior to those of others?

I guess… yes, during that time I did. I really believed my heritage quilt ideas were special, like they could put our little town on the map. It felt like I’d found something only I could make happen.
Do you feel like you need to control the outcome of events or projects you're involved in?
Yes… I think so. With the historical society fundraiser, I kind of took it over. I was making quilt designs, calling volunteers, setting schedules… promising things I really couldn’t keep up with.
Do you often feel like you're destined for greatness or that you have a special role to play in the world?
I don’t know about “destined for greatness,” exactly… but yes, I did feel like those quilt ideas could make our town known. Like I’d finally found the one thing only I could really make happen.
Do you think you would have felt extremely disappointed in yourself if the fundraiser hadn't turned out as planned?
Yes… I think I would have. I already keep going over the late orders and the things I said to the volunteers. I tell myself I let the church, the historical society… the whole town down, really.

Do you think your efforts with the historical society fundraiser were motivated more by a desire to achieve something perfect or by a belief that you were the only one who could make it truly successful?

Probably the second one… though I don’t like saying it that way. I really did believe those heritage quilt ideas could put our little town on the map, like I’d found the thing only I could make happen.
